input.quote: 11.2 Termination. If either party materially breaches any term or condition of this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within-thirty (30) days after receiving written notice of the breach, the nonbreaching party may terminate this Agreement on written notice at any time following the end of such-thirty (30) day period.
input.rationale: The Agreement runs for an initial five (5) year term (§ 11.1) and the only exit rights are for uncured material breach or insolvency (§ 11.2); there is no Corio right to terminate for convenience anywhere in the document (no Order Form structure exists, and no termination fee or refund mechanic applies outside the acceptance, warranty and IP-indemnity remedies). Absence of any Customer convenience right in a multi-year term fails both the preferred and fallback positions, so we propose the preferred position: convenience termination on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, plus confirmation that Commerce One has no mid-term convenience exit. The § 11.1 non-renewal right on 30 days' notice before term end is natural-term non-renewal (a RENEWAL matter), not a Vendor mid-term convenience right, so it is not flagged here.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.

proposal.summary: Add Corio termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and confirm Commerce One has no mid-term convenience exit.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 11 locks us into a five-year term with exit rights only for breach or insolvency, so we have added a convenience termination right on thirty (30) days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and confirmed Commerce One has no mid-term convenience exit. If you prefer, we can move to our fallback of 60-90 days' notice with an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees.

ops.text: Termination for Convenience. Corio may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One, in which case Commerce One shall refund to Corio, pro rata, any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination. Commerce One shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the initial five (5) year term or any renewal term.
